rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM Track;
rows.note: Assuming "in the catalog" means every row in the Track table.

rows.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT ar.ArtistId, ar.Name, COUNT(al.AlbumId) AS AlbumCount
  FROM Artist ar
  JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
  GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name
)
SELECT Name, AlbumCount
FROM counts
WHERE AlbumCount = (SELECT MAX(AlbumCount) FROM counts);
rows.note: Assumption: "most albums" means the count of rows in Album per artist, and I'll return only the top artist (all ties included).

rows.sql: SELECT Country, COUNT(*) AS CustomerCount FROM Customer GROUP BY Country ORDER BY CustomerCount DESC
rows.note: Assumption: count all rows in Customer grouped by the Country column, including any NULL country as its own group.

rows.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS Year, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS TotalRevenue FROM Invoice GROUP BY Year ORDER BY Year;
rows.note: Assumption: total revenue is the sum of Invoice.Total grouped by calendar year of InvoiceDate.

rows.sql: SELECT c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS FullName, ROUND(SUM(i.Total), 2) AS TotalSpent FROM Customer c JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId, c.FirstName, c.LastName ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC LIMIT 5
rows.note:
Plan: sum Invoice.Total per customer, join to Customer for full name, take the top 5 by total.

Assumption: "amount spent" is the sum of Invoice.Total across all invoices.

rows.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName, COUNT(c.CustomerId) AS n
  FROM Employee e
  JOIN Customer c ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId
  GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, FullName
)
SELECT FullName, n AS CustomerCount
FROM counts
WHERE n = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM counts);
rows.note: Assumption: "support rep" means the Employee referenced by Customer.SupportRepId, and I'll return only the top employee(s) by customer count.

rows.sql: SELECT p.PlaylistId, p.Name, COUNT(pt.TrackId) AS TrackCount FROM Playlist p LEFT JOIN PlaylistTrack pt ON pt.PlaylistId = p.PlaylistId WHERE p.Name = 'Grunge' GROUP BY p.PlaylistId, p.Name;
rows.note: I'm assuming the playlist is named exactly "Grunge" and counting its rows in PlaylistTrack.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS never_purchased_tracks FROM Track t WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM InvoiceLine il WHERE il.TrackId = t.TrackId);
rows.note: Assumption: "never been purchased" means the track does not appear in any InvoiceLine.

rows.sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT BillingCountry, SUM(Total) AS Revenue
  FROM Invoice
  WHERE InvoiceDate >= '2012-01-01' AND InvoiceDate < '2013-01-01'
  GROUP BY BillingCountry
)
SELECT BillingCountry, ROUND(Revenue, 2) AS Revenue
FROM rev
WHERE Revenue = (SELECT MAX(Revenue) FROM rev);
rows.note:
Plan: sum Invoice.Total by BillingCountry for invoices dated in 2012, then keep only the top country (ties included).

Assumption: revenue means the sum of invoice Total values.

rows.sql:
SELECT ar.Name
FROM Artist ar
JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
JOIN Track t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
WHERE t.GenreId IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 3;
rows.note: Assumption: a track's genre comes from Track.GenreId, and an artist's tracks are reached through Album.ArtistId.

rows.sql:
WITH genre_rev AS (
  SELECT g.Name AS Genre, SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) AS Revenue
  FROM InvoiceLine il
  JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
  JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
  GROUP BY g.Name
)
SELECT Genre,
       ROUND(100.0 * Revenue / (SELECT SUM(Revenue) FROM genre_rev), 2) AS Percentage
FROM genre_rev
ORDER BY Percentage DESC;
rows.note: Assumption: revenue is `UnitPrice * Quantity` from InvoiceLine, and each percentage is that genre's share of the total across all genres.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT i.CustomerId) AS customer_count
FROM Invoice i
JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
WHERE g.Name = 'Rock'
  AND i.CustomerId NOT IN (
    SELECT i2.CustomerId
    FROM Invoice i2
    JOIN InvoiceLine il2 ON il2.InvoiceId = i2.InvoiceId
    JOIN Track t2 ON t2.TrackId = il2.TrackId
    JOIN Genre g2 ON g2.GenreId = t2.GenreId
    WHERE g2.Name = 'Jazz'
  );
rows.note: Assumption: "bought" means the customer appears on an invoice containing a track whose genre is Rock (or Jazz).

rows.sql: SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) AS month, SUM(Total) AS revenue FROM Invoice WHERE strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2011' GROUP BY month ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: I'll sum invoice totals by month for 2011 and take the top month.
Assumption: "full name" means FirstName and LastName from the Employee table, and an employee with no customers is one with no Customer row whose SupportRepId matches their EmployeeId.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_first_purchase_2010 FROM (SELECT CustomerId, MIN(InvoiceDate) AS first_date FROM Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId) WHERE first_date >= '2010-01-01' AND first_date < '2011-01-01'
rows.note: Assumption: a customer's first purchase is their earliest invoice date, counted if that date falls in 2010.

rows.sql: SELECT al.Title, ROUND(SUM(t.Milliseconds) / 60000.0, 1) AS Minutes FROM Album al JOIN Track t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId GROUP BY al.AlbumId, al.Title ORDER BY SUM(t.Milliseconds) DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: Plan: sum track Milliseconds per album, take the top album, and convert to minutes (ms / 60000) rounded to 1 decimal.

rows.sql:
WITH yearly AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS year, SUM(Total) AS revenue
  FROM Invoice
  GROUP BY year
),
withprev AS (
  SELECT year, revenue, LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY year) AS prev_revenue
  FROM yearly
)
SELECT year,
       revenue,
       prev_revenue,
       ROUND((revenue - prev_revenue) * 100.0 / prev_revenue, 1) AS yoy_pct_change
FROM withprev
WHERE prev_revenue IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY year;
rows.note: Plan: sum `Invoice.Total` by calendar year, then compare each year with the previous one using `LAG`, rounding the percentage change to 1 decimal.

rows.sql:
WITH cust_totals AS (
  SELECT CustomerId, SUM(Total) AS total_spend
  FROM Invoice
  GROUP BY CustomerId
),
avg_spend AS (
  SELECT AVG(total_spend) AS avg_total FROM cust_totals
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_above_average
FROM cust_totals, avg_spend
WHERE cust_totals.total_spend > avg_spend.avg_total;
rows.note: I'll treat each customer's spend as the sum of their invoice totals, and the average as the mean of those per-customer sums across customers with at least one invoice.

rows.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT p.Name AS PlaylistName, COUNT(DISTINCT al.ArtistId) AS ArtistCount
  FROM Playlist p
  JOIN PlaylistTrack pt ON pt.PlaylistId = p.PlaylistId
  JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = pt.TrackId
  JOIN Album al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
  GROUP BY p.PlaylistId, p.Name
)
SELECT PlaylistName, ArtistCount
FROM counts
WHERE ArtistCount = (SELECT MAX(ArtistCount) FROM counts);
rows.note: Plan: join PlaylistTrack → Track → Album → Artist, count distinct artists per playlist, and keep the top playlist(s) (ties included).

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS invoice_count FROM (SELECT il.InvoiceId FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId GROUP BY il.InvoiceId HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 1) AS multi;
rows.note: Plan: join InvoiceLine to Track to get each invoice's genres, count distinct genres per invoice, and count invoices with more than one.

rows.sql:
WITH rep_revenue AS (
  SELECT e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS RepName, SUM(i.Total) AS Revenue
  FROM Invoice i
  JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId
  JOIN Employee e ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId
  WHERE strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) = '2010'
  GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, RepName
)
SELECT RepName, ROUND(Revenue, 2) AS Revenue
FROM rep_revenue
WHERE Revenue = (SELECT MAX(Revenue) FROM rep_revenue);
rows.note: I'm assuming revenue means the sum of `Invoice.Total` for invoices dated in 2010, grouped by each customer's support rep.

rows.sql:
WITH yearly AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) AS Year,
         g.Name AS Genre,
         SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) AS Revenue
  FROM InvoiceLine il
  JOIN Invoice i ON i.InvoiceId = il.InvoiceId
  JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
  JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
  GROUP BY Year, Genre
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT Year, Genre, Revenue,
         RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY Year ORDER BY Revenue DESC) AS rnk
  FROM yearly
)
SELECT Year, Genre, ROUND(Revenue, 2) AS Revenue
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk = 2
ORDER BY Year;
rows.note: Assumption: revenue is UnitPrice × Quantity from InvoiceLine, grouped by the invoice year, and a tie for second place returns all tied genres.

rows.sql:
WITH t AS (
  SELECT CustomerId,
    SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2012' THEN Total ELSE 0 END) AS s2012,
    SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2013' THEN Total ELSE 0 END) AS s2013
  FROM Invoice
  GROUP BY CustomerId
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_spent_more_in_2013
FROM t
WHERE s2013 > s2012;
rows.note:
Plan: compute each customer's total invoice amount for 2012 and 2013 from Invoice.Total, then count customers where the 2013 total exceeds the 2012 total (customers with no invoices in a year count as 0).

Assumption: "spent" means the sum of Invoice.Total by InvoiceDate year.

rows.sql:
WITH ordered AS (
  SELECT Total, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY Total) AS rn, COUNT(*) OVER () AS cnt
  FROM Invoice
)
SELECT AVG(Total) AS median_total
FROM ordered
WHERE rn IN ((cnt + 1) / 2, (cnt + 2) / 2);
rows.note: Assumption: the median is taken over all rows in the Invoice table's Total column, with the average of the two middle values when the count is even.

rows.sql:
WITH artist_playlists AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ar.ArtistId, ar.Name AS ArtistName, pt.PlaylistId
  FROM PlaylistTrack pt
  JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = pt.TrackId
  JOIN Album al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
  JOIN Artist ar ON ar.ArtistId = al.ArtistId
),
counts AS (
  SELECT ArtistId, ArtistName, COUNT(*) AS DistinctPlaylists
  FROM artist_playlists
  GROUP BY ArtistId, ArtistName
)
SELECT ArtistName, DistinctPlaylists
FROM counts
WHERE DistinctPlaylists = (SELECT MAX(DistinctPlaylists) FROM counts);
rows.note: Assumption: an artist's playlists are those containing at least one of their tracks, counted via Track → Album → Artist, and all tied artists are returned.

rows.sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(cnt), 2) AS avg_line_items_per_invoice
FROM (
  SELECT i.InvoiceId, COUNT(il.InvoiceLineId) AS cnt
  FROM Invoice i
  LEFT JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
  GROUP BY i.InvoiceId
) t;
rows.note: Assumption: line items are rows in InvoiceLine, and the average is over all invoices (including any with zero lines, if they exist).

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS discontinued_products FROM Products WHERE Discontinued = '1';
rows.note: Assumption: Discontinued = '1' in Products.Discontinued.

rows.sql: SELECT CompanyName FROM Suppliers WHERE Country = 'Germany';
rows.note: I'll filter the Suppliers table on `Country = 'Germany'` and return the company names.

rows.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT c.CategoryName, COUNT(p.ProductID) AS ProductCount
  FROM Categories c
  JOIN Products p ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID
  GROUP BY c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName
)
SELECT CategoryName, ProductCount
FROM counts
WHERE ProductCount = (SELECT MAX(ProductCount) FROM counts);
rows.note: I'll count products per category by `CategoryID` and return every category tied for the highest count.

rows.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', OrderDate) AS Year, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount FROM Orders GROUP BY Year ORDER BY Year;
rows.note: Assumption: "placed" means OrderDate, grouped by calendar year.

rows.sql: SELECT s.CompanyName AS ShipperName, ROUND(AVG(o.Freight), 2) AS AverageFreight FROM Orders o JOIN Shippers s ON o.ShipVia = s.ShipperID GROUP BY s.ShipperID, s.CompanyName;
rows.note: Assumption: average freight is taken over all orders per shipper, joining Orders.ShipVia to Shippers.ShipperID.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName FROM Employees e WHERE e.ReportsTo = (SELECT EmployeeID FROM Employees WHERE FirstName = 'Andrew' AND LastName = 'Fuller')
rows.note: I'll assume Andrew Fuller is the employee with FirstName 'Andrew' and LastName 'Fuller', and list everyone whose ReportsTo matches his EmployeeID.

rows.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT EmployeeID, COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM Orders
  WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2020'
  GROUP BY EmployeeID
),
top AS (
  SELECT MAX(order_count) AS max_count FROM counts
)
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS full_name, c.order_count
FROM counts c
JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = c.EmployeeID
WHERE c.order_count = (SELECT max_count FROM top);
rows.note: Assumption: "in 2020" means OrderDate falls within calendar year 2020, and "full name" means FirstName plus LastName.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS num_products FROM Products WHERE UnitPrice > (SELECT AVG(UnitPrice) FROM Products);
rows.note: Assumption: "average product unit price" is the simple average of Products.UnitPrice across all products.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS OrdersShippedToFrance FROM Orders WHERE ShipCountry = 'France';
rows.note: Assumption: "shipped to France" means ShipCountry = 'France' on the Orders table, counting all orders regardless of whether ShippedDate is filled in.

rows.sql:
SELECT p.ProductName AS product_name,
       ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS revenue
FROM "Order Details" od
JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID
GROUP BY p.ProductID, p.ProductName
ORDER BY revenue DESC
LIMIT 5;
rows.note:
Plan: compute revenue per product as sum of UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) from "Order Details", join to Products for names, take the top 5 by revenue, and round to 2 decimals.

Assumption: revenue uses the line-level UnitPrice from Order Details (not the current Products price).

rows.sql:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT c.CategoryName, p.ProductName, p.UnitPrice,
         RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY c.CategoryID ORDER BY p.UnitPrice DESC) AS rk
  FROM Products p
  JOIN Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID
)
SELECT CategoryName, ProductName, UnitPrice
FROM ranked
WHERE rk = 1
ORDER BY CategoryName;
rows.note: I'll use each product's `UnitPrice` from `Products`, joined to `Categories`, and keep all products tied for the highest price in each category.

rows.sql:
WITH cust_rev AS (
  SELECT c.CompanyName, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS revenue
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
  JOIN Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
  WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2021'
  GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.CompanyName
)
SELECT CompanyName, revenue
FROM cust_rev
WHERE revenue = (SELECT MAX(revenue) FROM cust_rev);
rows.note: Assumption: revenue is SUM(UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount)) over order lines, grouped by customer, using orders dated in 2021.

rows.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS month_num, COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM Orders
  WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2021'
  GROUP BY month_num
)
SELECT month_num, order_count
FROM counts
WHERE order_count = (SELECT MAX(order_count) FROM counts);
rows.note: I'll count orders by calendar month of `OrderDate` for 2021 and return the top month, including any ties.
The Orders table has no orders dated in 1997. Order dates run from 2012-07-10 to 2023-10-28, so the question can't be answered from this database.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS late_shipped_orders FROM Orders WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL AND ShippedDate > RequiredDate;
rows.note: Assumption: "shipped after required date" means ShippedDate is not NULL and ShippedDate > RequiredDate.

rows.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(julianday(ShippedDate) - julianday(OrderDate)), 1) AS avg_days_to_ship FROM Orders WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL;
rows.note: Assumption: "shipped orders" means orders with a non-NULL ShippedDate, and the average is over the difference in days between ShippedDate and OrderDate.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM Products WHERE Discontinued = '0' AND UnitsInStock < ReorderLevel;
rows.note: Assumption: "still sold" means Discontinued = '0', and "below reorder level" means UnitsInStock < ReorderLevel.

rows.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT c.Country, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN Customers c ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
  WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2019'
  GROUP BY c.Country
)
SELECT Country, OrderCount
FROM counts
WHERE OrderCount = (SELECT MAX(OrderCount) FROM counts);
rows.note: Assumption: "placed in 2019" means the order's OrderDate falls in calendar year 2019, and the country is the customer's country from the Customers table.

rows.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN c.CategoryName = 'Beverages' THEN od."UnitPrice" * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount) ELSE 0 END) / SUM(od."UnitPrice" * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 1) AS beverages_pct_2023 FROM "Order Details" od JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID JOIN Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2023';
rows.note: Assumption: revenue is UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) from Order Details, and 2023 is based on OrderDate.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM (SELECT CustomerID FROM Orders WHERE OrderDate >= '2020-01-01' AND OrderDate < '2021-01-01' GROUP BY CustomerID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT strftime('%m', OrderDate)) = 12) AS t;
rows.note: Assumption: a customer qualifies if they have at least one order in each of the 12 calendar months of 2020, based on OrderDate.

rows.sql:
WITH order_values AS (
  SELECT o.OrderID, o.EmployeeID, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS order_value
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
  GROUP BY o.OrderID, o.EmployeeID
),
emp_avg AS (
  SELECT EmployeeID, AVG(order_value) AS avg_order_value
  FROM order_values
  GROUP BY EmployeeID
)
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS full_name, ea.avg_order_value
FROM emp_avg ea
JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = ea.EmployeeID
WHERE ea.avg_order_value = (SELECT MAX(avg_order_value) FROM emp_avg);
rows.note: Assumption: each order's value is the sum of UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) across its lines, and each employee's average is taken over their own orders.

rows.sql:
WITH supplier_revenue AS (
  SELECT s.CompanyName, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS Revenue
  FROM "Order Details" od
  JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
  JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID
  JOIN Suppliers s ON s.SupplierID = p.SupplierID
  WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2018'
  GROUP BY s.SupplierID, s.CompanyName
)
SELECT CompanyName, Revenue
FROM supplier_revenue
WHERE Revenue = (SELECT MAX(Revenue) FROM supplier_revenue);
rows.note: Assumption: revenue is UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) from Order Details, filtered to orders dated in 2018, summed by supplier. I'll return only the top supplier, including any tie.

rows.sql:
WITH yearly AS (
  SELECT od.ProductID,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2021' THEN od.Quantity ELSE 0 END) AS units_2021,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2022' THEN od.Quantity ELSE 0 END) AS units_2022
  FROM "Order Details" od
  JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
  GROUP BY od.ProductID
),
diff AS (
  SELECT y.ProductID, p.ProductName, y.units_2021, y.units_2022,
         y.units_2022 - y.units_2021 AS increase
  FROM yearly y
  JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = y.ProductID
)
SELECT ProductName, units_2021, units_2022, increase
FROM diff
WHERE increase = (SELECT MAX(increase) FROM diff);
rows.note: Assumption: units sold = sum of `Quantity` from `Order Details`, grouped by the year of `Orders.OrderDate`, and the largest increase is 2022 minus 2021.

rows.sql:
SELECT s.CompanyName AS ShipperName,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN o.ShippedDate > o.RequiredDate THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS LatePercentage
FROM Orders o
JOIN Shippers s ON s.ShipperID = o.ShipVia
WHERE o.ShippedDate IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY s.ShipperID, s.CompanyName
ORDER BY s.CompanyName;
rows.note: I'll treat "shipped orders" as orders with a non-NULL ShippedDate, and "late" as ShippedDate later than RequiredDate.

rows.sql:
WITH yearly AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y', OrderDate) AS year, COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM Orders
  GROUP BY strftime('%Y', OrderDate)
)
SELECT year,
       SUM(order_count) OVER (ORDER BY year ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_order_count
FROM yearly
ORDER BY year;
rows.note:
Plan: count orders per year from Orders.OrderDate, then add a running total ordered by year.

Assumption: "running total of orders by year" means the count of orders per calendar year (from OrderDate), accumulated across years.

rows.sql:
WITH order_totals AS (
  SELECT OrderID, SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)) AS total_value
  FROM "Order Details"
  GROUP BY OrderID
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_over_10000
FROM order_totals
WHERE total_value > 10000;
rows.note: I'll treat each order's total as the sum of UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) over its line items, and count orders where that total exceeds 10,000.

rows.sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT o.EmployeeID,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2018' THEN od."UnitPrice" * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount) ELSE 0 END) AS rev2018,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2019' THEN od."UnitPrice" * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount) ELSE 0 END) AS rev2019
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
  GROUP BY o.EmployeeID
),
diff AS (
  SELECT EmployeeID, rev2018, rev2019, (rev2019 - rev2018) AS growth FROM rev
)
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName, d.rev2018, d.rev2019, d.growth
FROM diff d
JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = d.EmployeeID
WHERE d.growth = (SELECT MAX(growth) FROM diff);
rows.note: Assumption: revenue is SUM(UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount)) by the order's OrderDate year, and "grew the most" means the largest 2019 minus 2018 difference. Ties are all returned.
